h: Ferries, Football and a Final Showdown
p: Liverpool is a city that wears its heart on its sleeve. It's proud of its music, its football, its humour and its waterfront, and it welcomes visitors with open arms. A night out here can go in any direction, which is half the fun, but it helps to have a starting point that gets everyone in the mood. A games bar does exactly that.

Lime Street station brings you right into the city centre, with fast trains from London, Manchester and beyond, and the Merseyrail network links the centre with the Wirral, Southport and the surrounding towns. Much of the centre is walkable, from the shops of Liverpool ONE to the waterfront.

If you're planning a big group night, booking early is key. Liverpool is hugely popular for hen and stag weekends, as well as for gig nights and matchdays, so bars fill up quickly. Mix your teams so the competitive ones are spread out, and keep the scoreboard on show for maximum banter.

During the day, the Mersey Ferry is a must, giving you that classic view of the Three Graces and the waterfront from the river. The Walker Art Gallery and World Museum, both on William Brown Street near Lime Street, are free to visit and full of treasures. For something different, the Western Approaches museum tells the story of the secret wartime headquarters that ran the Battle of the Atlantic from beneath the city streets. After all that, a few hours of games makes the perfect way to round off the day.
